title: Tenali Raman and the Midnight Lake of Ice
summary: A wealthy, tyrannical landlord named Somappa made a cruel bet with a poor tenant farmer named Somu, who owed thirty bags of grain: 'If thou canst stand in the frozen temple tank...
full_text:
A wealthy, tyrannical landlord named Somappa made a cruel bet with a poor tenant farmer named Somu, who owed thirty bags of grain:
'If thou canst stand in the frozen temple tank up to thy waist for the entire night from dusk to dawn without warm clothes, thy debt shall be forgiven! If thou failest, I shall seize thy children as bonded servants!'

Desperate to protect his family, Somu stood in the freezing water all night, his limbs turning blue, his teeth chattering in agony.
At dawn, Somu crawled out alive and demanded the debt receipt.
The cruel landlord refused, sneering:
'Thou didst look at the burning cremation fire on the distant hill! Thou wert warmed by the smoke! Thy debt stands!'

Somu came weeping to Tenali Raman.
Tenali’s heart burned with righteous fury at the landlord’s cruelty.

Tenali invited Landlord Somappa to a grand banquet at his house that evening.
Somappa arrived, expecting rich dishes.
Instead, Tenali led Somappa into his garden, where an open stone pool was filled with ice-cold mountain water.
Tenali’s burly servants seized the landlord, stripped him of his velvet coat, and placed him in the freezing water!

Somappa shrieked, shivering and weeping:
'Tenali! What madness is this? I am freezing to death! Release me!'

Tenali sat fifty yards away on a terrace beside a roaring charcoal fire, roasting succulent sweet potatoes and sipping hot spiced tea.
Tenali called out cheerfully:
'Why dost thou complain, friend Somappa? Look at my roaring charcoal fire fifty yards away!
According to thy own legal theory, the heat from my fire is blowing across the grass and thoroughly warming thee in the water!
Stay in the tank until sunrise, and thou shalt be as warm as a roast pheasant!'

Somappa’s teeth chattered violently, his lips turned blue, and he screamed in agonizing repentance:
'Mercy, Tenali! I was a monster! I lied! Fire fifty yards away cannot warm a man freezing in icy water!
Release me! I forgive Somu’s debt forever, and I will give him the land deed as a gift!'

Tenali had the legal debt release and land deed signed on the spot by Somappa’s trembling hands before pulling him from the pool.
Tenali wrapped the shivering landlord in a blanket, fed him hot ginger tea, and said:
'Never impose a cruelty upon another man that thine own soft flesh cannot endure for ten minutes.'

Somu received his freedom and his land, while Somappa became a humble, generous man, cured of his tyranny forever.
moral: Cruelty cloaked in impossible wagers is defeated when the tyrant is forced to feel the cold truth.
